author: BBC News
description:
A man suspected of carrying out a terror rampage at a Berlin Pride event has been shot dead by police.

German police say officers fired at Abdul Ballout after he rushed towards them with a knife.  They say he died at the scene.  

Prosecutors say that Ballout drove a van into a crowd and stabbed multiple people in an attack that left one woman dead and at least 29 injured. 

Ballout was a 21-year-old German citizen of Lebanese background who was known to police and is said to have tried to join the Islamic State group. 

Germany’s interior minister said that he could not rule out the possibility of copycat attacks and announced that the country's threat level was being raised.

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Joe Inwood.

One woman is dead and 29 others are injured after a car was driven into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event on Saturday night. Multiple people were then stabbed with a blade that “might have been a machete”.
 
Police have identified a suspect named Abdul Ballout, a German citizen of Lebanese background who was known to police and previously had “committed a number of crimes”.
 
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says extremists "have no place in our society", vowing to do everything in the government's power to see justice served.

author: BBC News
description:
One woman is dead and 16 others are injured after a car was driven into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event, police say.

Police have identified a suspect, who they say has known links to Islamist circles, but say no arrests have been made.

An intensive manhunt is under way in the German capital - officers have released a photo of the suspect and are appealing for help finding him.

A white vehicle suspected of being used in the attack has also been pictured inside the police cordon.
